A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Similarity Kernel Mixup work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification and regression experiments, toy examples, efficiency measurements and appendix ablations, alongside explicitly attributed external results.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds corruption and out-of-distribution evaluations, ViT results, diagnostic experiments and method comparisons.

M1.justification: The original similarity kernel, warping equations and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. v3 adds adaptations: SK RegMixup uses SK mixing as a regularization term, while SK CutMix makes CutMix's Beta distribution depend on pair similarity (Section 4.2 and Appendices H and M).

E1.justification: v3 adds CIFAR10-C and CIFAR100-C corruption testing and ImageNet-R and ImageNet-A out-of-distribution evaluation. Earlier classification, regression and toy datasets remain covered; Circles moves to Appendix I rather than being removed.

E2.justification: v3 evaluates a simpler distance-dependent two-Beta baseline and CutMix in Appendices L and M. It replaces cited RegMixup classification results with reproduced comparisons and expands the image-classification efficiency comparison to include Mixup, RegMixup and CutMix, substantially broadening the controls.

E3.justification: New protocols include ViT-S/16 training for 300 epochs with AdamW, corruption evaluation averaged across corruption types and severities, and a ResNet18 diagnostic using 10,000 mixed test samples. The earlier ResNet and regression training settings largely remain unchanged; these are added evaluation designs.

E4.justification: Figures 1a and 2b newly test label agreement versus mixing distance and whether SK mixing mitigates disagreement. v3 also adds distribution-shift robustness tests, a coarse two-distribution alternative testing the need for fine-grained adaptation, and nonlinear-mixing analysis. Earlier hyperparameter, warping-function and distance-space ablations are retained.

E5.justification: The stated four classification runs and ten regression runs remain unchanged. However, v3 Table 4 drops the standard deviations accompanying the retained ImageNet/ResNet50 results in v2 Table 3. This reduces uncertainty reporting without establishing that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive results for shifted datasets, ViTs, method combinations and new controls. Existing entries also change: Table 2's reproduced CIFAR100/ResNet101 ERM accuracy changes from 77.99 ± 0.31 to 74.27 ± 0.37 without an explained protocol change. Conversely, v2 Table 1 is retained as v3 Table 9, and the regression results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 introduces disjoint bounded-support class-manifold assumptions, Theorem 3.1 on off-manifold interpolation, and Theorem 3.2 proposing a Wasserstein-based lower bound on label-noise probability. Appendix F adds their proofs and probability-metric definitions and lemmas. The earlier inverse-transform-sampling proposition and proof are retained.

C1.justification: v3 expands the claimed contributions to a theoretical distance–label-noise relationship, out-of-distribution improvements and demonstrated combination with RegMixup. v2 presents distance primarily as motivation and emphasizes the performance–calibration trade-off. The abstract, contribution list and conclusion reflect this broader scope.

C2.justification: v3 develops manifold mismatch as a broader mechanism encompassing intrusion and samples outside original class manifolds, and interprets the new label-agreement diagnostics through it. Appendices L and M add explanations about coarse-baseline parameter sensitivity and limits of transferring linear-mixing calibration benefits to CutMix. The existing limitations in Appendix B largely remain.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds ViT optimizer, schedule, batch-size and GPU details, plus the SK RegMixup setting tau_max = 10. The new diagnostic's sampling procedure is also documented. Most earlier implementation information is retained, and the code-access URL is unchanged despite relocation.

R1.justification: v3 adds references and discussion concerning noisy augmentation, mixup theory, manifold learning and robustness. It substantively revises k-Mixup's description to optimal-transport pair selection and removes the Snoek warping reference. The overall related-work organization and calibration-focused positioning remain recognizable.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and substantial portions of the prose remain intact. v3 revises the motivation and manifold terminology, relocates explanatory and efficiency discussion, reorganizes appendices, and adds a reproducibility statement, acknowledgements and updated author/publication text.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the introductory schematic and warping-function panel with diagnostic plots, separates the Moons and Circles illustrations, and redistributes calibration results between main and appendix tables. New robustness and variant tables substantially expand the displays. The quantile plot also switches to already-reported median-based, unscaled results.

improvement.justification: The new robustness evaluations, ViT experiments and simpler-baseline comparisons materially strengthen empirical support. However, v3 promotes the distance–noise intuition to a proved central claim while Appendix F.2 uses unsupported equalities between total-variation distances involving the mixed-point and endpoint label distributions; subsequent expressions proportional to lambda and 1−lambda need not be equal. ImageNet standard deviations are also removed. These substantive benefits and weaknesses leave the net quality change uncertain.
